caption: Eval-mode generalisation gap for all seven full-data runs. Pre-investigation Adam baseline overfits (0.337) and SAM ρ=0.01–0.2 fails to help; the investigation's ρ=0.5+WD run collapses the gap to 0.049.
caveats: Pre-investigation runs used the reverse-early-stopping rule; the two investigation runs used val-loss-plateau. Cross-phase gap comparison is directional; the clean matched pair is Adam+WD vs SAM ρ=0.5+WD.

caption: Full-data generalisation gap as a function of SAM's ρ. Below ρ≈0.2 the perturbation is too small to matter (gap ≈ baseline); ρ=0.5 (with WD) is where the gap collapses.
caveats: The ρ=0.5 point also switches WD from 0 to 1e-3 and uses a different stopping rule, so it is not a pure ρ-only comparison — see the decomposition figure.

caption: Decomposition of the total gap reduction (0.337 → 0.049): weight decay accounts for ~28%, SAM ρ=0.5 for ~72%.
caveats: The Adam-baseline → Adam+WD step also carries the stopping-rule change (reverse-early-stop → val-plateau); the Adam+WD → SAM+WD step is the clean matched pair (single variable: the SAM wrapper).

caption: Each run as a point in (gap, val R²) space. SAM ρ=0.5+WD moves far left (gap 0.049) for a ~0.012 R² cost vs the baseline; Adam+WD sits between.
caveats: Mixed stopping rules across points (see per-condition table).

caption: Pre-investigation training curves. Adding SAM at ρ≤0.2 leaves the train/val separation essentially unchanged — the observation that opened the investigation.
caveats: Train-mode per-epoch losses (not eval-mode); early epochs show spuriously negative gaps as BN statistics settle.

caption: Investigation training curves. Under SAM ρ=0.5+WD the train and val curves track each other closely for the whole run; Adam+WD narrows the separation partially; the baseline's curves stay far apart.
caveats: Different stopping rules and epoch counts (90 / 157 / 250). Train-mode losses.

caption: Per-epoch gap trajectories. SAM ρ=0.5+WD (right) holds the gap near zero from early on; the pre-investigation SAM sweep (left) widens toward the baseline's ~0.3–0.4.
caveats: Train-mode per-epoch gap; noisier than the eval-mode final numbers and can be negative early while BN statistics stabilise.

caption: Train/val/test R² per condition (y-axis zoomed). Every pre-investigation run and Adam+WD keep train R² ≈ 0.90 well above val ≈ 0.86; SAM ρ=0.5+WD is the only run whose train R² (0.852) sits right on top of its val R² (0.844) — the visual signature of the closed gap.
caveats: Adam+WD (Stage 4b) recorded val R² only — train/test bars are absent for it.

caption: Train/val/test RMSE per condition (y-axis zoomed). Same story as R²: under SAM ρ=0.5+WD train RMSE rises toward the val level rather than val error dropping toward train.
Final eval-mode loss on each split. The train/val separation IS the generalisation gap; it is visibly smallest for SAM ρ=0.5+WD.
Stage 3 sweep grid. Gap falls monotonically with ρ and with WD=1e-3; val R² also falls at high ρ on the subsample (a subsample artefact — see Stage 3 notes).
caveats: 10% subsample: absolute gap values are inflated and not comparable to full-data numbers; only the ordering across cells is used.

caption: Stage 3 subsample gap vs ρ, split by weight decay. Both levers reduce the gap; they combine roughly additively, motivating the ρ=0.5 + WD=1e-3 pick.
caveats: Subsample gaps are inflated vs full data; qualitative trend only.

caption: 1-D filter-normalised loss landscape (Li et al. 2018 style), mean ± sd over 3 random directions, on 8000-row subsamples, span ±0.06. A shallower rise away from α=0 and a smaller train–val separation indicate a flatter minimum that generalises better. Curves that leave the top of the axis have escaped the basin within this α range.
caveats: BN running statistics are held fixed while weights are perturbed (Li et al. recommend recomputing them); per-tensor (not per-filter) normalisation, so α is only comparable within this figure; single 1-D slice family; subsampled data. Read alongside figure 15 (Hessian λ_max).

caption: Largest Hessian eigenvalue of the training loss at each trained solution (power iteration, 25 steps, 8192-sample batch). Lower = flatter minimum. This is the quantitative companion to the landscape figure.
caveats: Single batch, single random init for power iteration; eigenvalue scale is relative, compare across bars not to an absolute reference. BN in eval mode.

caption: Predicted vs true ln IC50 on the val split, Adam baseline vs SAM ρ=0.5+WD. Comparable predictive accuracy; SAM's advantage is the generalisation gap, not raw val accuracy.
caveats: SAM ρ=0.5 predictions regenerated from the rerun checkpoint; baseline predictions are the committed parquet.
